name: indie_portfolio
archetype: Indie software developer and designer personal portfolio
market: Tech industry recruiters, potential clients, open source community
density: Sparse and intentional. Each project gets its own space. No visual clutter. The terminal and code aesthetic influences the design without being a cliché. Cursor blinking in the hero. A sense of craft and personality rather than corporate polish.
nav_style: Minimal: name/handle as nav logo on left. Three or four text links only: Work, Writing, About, Contact. No borders, no background. The nav barely exists — content is the focus. Possibly a theme toggle (light/dark).
commercial_model: Personal brand. Not directly commercial. Available for freelance work. Open source contributor. Goal is credibility signaling to potential employers and collaborators.
color_palette: Dark theme with near-black (#0A0A0A) background. Soft white (#E8E8E8) text — not harsh pure white. Accent: electric green (#39FF14) — the terminal/hacker aesthetic personal brand color. Use this consistently for all links, highlights, active states, and the cursor blink. Secondary text #6B7280. Code syntax highlighting: keywords #61DAFB (cyan), strings #A8FF78 (lime), numbers #FFD700 (gold), comments #555555.
typography: Mix of identity and function. JetBrains Mono or Fira Code for the name and code-adjacent content. Inter or System UI for prose. Developer blogs often use markdown-rendered look. 'console.log(name)' style personal statement in the hero.

pages.title: Home
pages.description: Full-screen dark hero with terminal-style introduction: > Hi, I'm [Name]. Developer, designer, builder. Three featured projects below with screenshots. Tech stack icons strip. Currently building section. Writing/blog preview (2 recent posts). Contact CTA.

pages.title: Work
pages.description: Project portfolio grid. Each project: screenshot, name, one-line description, tech stack badges, links to GitHub and live demo. Featured project gets full-width treatment. Open source contributions section.

pages.title: Project Detail
pages.description: Single project page. Problem statement. Technical approach. Architecture diagram (CSS/SVG). Screenshots of the UI. Key technical decisions explained. Metrics/outcomes if available. Stack used. GitHub link.

pages.title: Writing
pages.description: Blog post list with date, title, reading time, and first line. Tags for filtering: React, Systems, Career, Open Source. Featured/pinned post at top. RSS feed link in footer.

pages.title: About
pages.description: Personal page. Photo. Current role and company. Background story. What I'm learning now. What I'm building on the side. Currently reading. Tools I use. Way too long and opinionated. Contact info and resume download.
